units.translation: There are no examples in Sophocles, but several in Euripides (see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2168.), in two of which Ασιάς [Asian] and Ασιάδες [Asian women] are required by the metre, while in the rest there is not sufficient reason why Ασιάδος [of Asia] and the remaining cases should be changed into Ἀσίδος [of Asia] for the sake of removing a tribrach or dactyl: an argument which has some force in Aeschylus, but scarcely any in Euripides.
You will come to the Asian mainland.
O cities of all the Asian land.
one man of all Asia (ἀσιάδος [of Asia] in some copies) rich in flocks,
of the Asian land (perhaps ὁ δ᾽ Ασίδος [but he of Asia]) mighty in flocks,
All the Asian land groans, being emptied,
he came from the land of Asia.
and he rushes through the lands of Asia.
For all the Asian-born strength has departed.

where I wrote Ασιάτις [Asian]. The tragedians seem to have used the form Ασιῆτις [Asian] in lyric passages, while in the rest they say Ασιάτης [Asian man] and Ασιάτις [Asian woman], although the manuscripts of Euripides sometimes introduce a in the one, sometimes in the other, as has been said in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2167.
No one of mortals will pass through life unharmed in all things.
and he passes through life unharmed.
Shall I rejoice and raise a cry for the city's unharmed savior fortune?
Who of mortals could ever pray to be born with an unharmed destiny?
How do you bid me practice wickedness?
For the gods are not heedless of those who have slain many,
and gladly would he bend his knee in his own home.
glad to come to the bridge that yokes two lands.
and for you, glad, the many-colored night will hide the light.
They themselves will guide you, and very gladly.
the wretched ones gasp on the dry land.

παρ' ἀσπίδος [by the shield] on the shield side, i.e. on the left side
Do you hear the clash of shields?
And the shield is fashioned in no small way.
I mean the circle of the shield.
the unharvested bronze of the shields (thus Blomfield for ἀθέριτον ἀσπίδος [unharvested of the shield]) stretched high.
For this man is no small shield of courage for us.
